aminonucle- oside-induced nephrosis in the rat is associated with a significant increase in the phosphorylation associated with the succinate oxidation in liver mitochondria.

aminonucle- oside is a potent inhibitor of oxidative phosphorylation in the submitochondrial fraction of rat liver, and a potent activator of the phosphorylation associated with the succinate oxidation of the rat liver mitochondria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the aminonucloside nephrosis is a disease of energy metabolism.
aminonucleotide-induced nephrosis is characterized by a marked increase of hepatic oxidative phosphorylation associated with the succinate dehydrogenase-cytochrome c reductase system.
the aminonudeoside-induced nephrotic rat is a useful model for the study of the pathophysiology of the human disease nephrotic syndrome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that the mitochondria are not only the powerhouse of the cells but also the control center for the cell.
aminonucleotide is a potent inhibitor of mitochondrial function.
the mitochondrial dysfunction is not the cause of the nephrosis, but it does occur as a secondary effect of the nephrosis.
